newsitem.title: UK: Racal Electronics sees lower profits.
newsitem.headline: Racal Electronics sees lower profits.

text.p: British electronics firm Racal Electronics said on Monday it expected its pre-tax profits for its first half to be 21 million stg, nearly 20 million below market expectations.
In a statement, the company said the dip in profits would be mainly due to a reduction in order intake in its Radio Group division.
Racal said lower orders would also result in an "operating loss" for the year in Radio Communications.
"Pretax profits for the full year are expected to be approximately 50 million stg after exceptional charges of 20 million stg," the statement said.
Racal's first-half pre-tax profit of 21 million stg would be after charging 10 million stg as exceptional costs incurred for reorganising the Data group, it said.
The Data group is expected to show half year losses, similar to the previous year, when the company announces its results on December 3.
But the group is expected to show profits in the second half, it said.
"With a substantial increase in profits from the Data Group the results in 1997/98 will be much improved," Racal said.
